evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI publicly described an AGI carve-out and board authority to determine attainment. This establishes the relevant licensing distinction, but not automatic termination of all existing rights or a requirement for skeptical experts.

evidence_items.publisher: Superior Court of California, County of San Francisco; copy hosted by Courthouse News Service
evidence_items.locator: Complaint paragraph 31; requested relief also appears in Prayer for Relief B–C
evidence_items.explanation: The complaint alleges that GPT-4 is AGI and requests a judicial determination placing it outside Microsoft's license. This establishes Musk's litigation position, not the truth of his allegation or the necessity of an expert defense.

The report documents both technical skepticism and possible legal weaknesses unrelated to proving whether GPT-4 is AGI. This cautions against treating skeptical experts as necessary; news reporting is used because no inspected primary record establishes that necessity.

unresolved_gaps: No inspected record establishes that OpenAI needed skeptical expert evidence to preserve its licensing position as of March 3, 2024.
The complete operative license was not obtained; the public description establishes an AGI carve-out rather than the asserted automatic termination mechanism.
The evidence does not identify a specific OpenAI claim of achieved AGI that its defense would need to retract.
